homePage.welcomeHeadline: A landmark church with an open door
homePage.welcomeBodyP1: Second Presbyterian is a National Historic Landmark on Michigan Avenue, home to nine Tiffany windows and a sanctuary built for worship. The building is remarkable. The people are the point.
homePage.welcomeBodyP2: We are a Reformed congregation in the Presbyterian Church (USA), and we welcome everyone: women and men, gay and straight, lifelong believers and the simply curious. Come as you are.
homePage.inclusiveStatement: Whoever you are, wherever you are on your journey of faith, you are welcome here.
homePage.inclusiveBody: We are an inclusive congregation, and we welcome the full participation of women and LGBTQ people in the life and leadership of the church.
homePage.involvedSubhead: Join us for worship, fellowship, study, art, and food. There is a place for you here.
homePage.recordBody: News, reflections, and what is coming up at Second, in your inbox.
homePage.eventsHeadline: There is always something happening at Second
homePage.eventsIntro: Worship, study, shared meals, music, and fellowship fill the week. A few of our weekly rhythms:
homePage.finalCtaHeadline: Whoever you are, you are welcome here.
homePage.finalCtaSubhead: Plan your first visit, or simply show up on Sunday. We will be glad you came.

worshipPage.serviceBodyP1: Our service follows a traditional, liturgical format, with hymns, spirituals, and anthems led by organ and choir. We celebrate the Eucharist on the first Sunday of each month.
worshipPage.serviceBodyP2: Come as you are. Casual attire is always welcome. There is no wrong way to be here, and no experience required.
worshipPage.planCard1Body: We are at 1936 South Michigan Ave in the South Loop, close to public transit, with first-come, first-served free parking.
worshipPage.planCard2Body: Whatever feels right to you. Some dress up, many do not. Come as you are.
worshipPage.planCard3Body: Children are welcome in worship, with a children's message and a cry room if you need it.
worshipPage.planCard4Body: The sanctuary is accessible. If you need any accommodation to join us, reach out and we will be glad to help.
worshipPage.kidsBodyP1: Little ones are part of the worshipping congregation at Second, and we welcome their noise and their needs. We keep books, coloring materials, and fidget toys on hand, and there is a children's message during the service.
worshipPage.kidsBodyP2: Need a quieter moment? A cry room with an audio stream of the service is always available.
worshipPage.quoteText: We are called to an everlasting preoccupation with God.
worshipPage.finalCtaSubhead: Have a question before Sunday? We would love to help you feel at home before you arrive.

beliefsPage.scriptureQuote: “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.”
beliefsPage.beliefsQ1A1: Humanity and all things, seen and unseen, were created by God out of the abundance of the divine love of the Trinity. Humanity is created in God's image, meaning that each person is invested with profound worth and dignity, and charged with authority to care for and serve creation as God does. We do not live out our identity as image-bearers, and like all things, without Christ we are captive to Sin and Death. But because we are created out of God's extraordinary love, Augustine of Hippo says, "Our hearts are restless until they find rest in you."
beliefsPage.beliefsQ2A1: God is love, eternally three Persons and one Being. God is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, each coeternal, consubstantial, and coequal with one another. God is revealed to us in Jesus Christ, who is fully God and fully human, incarnate by the power of the Holy Spirit and the courageous yes of Mary. Because of this, we know God as the One who gives himself. God is holy, complete within himself, all-powerful, all-knowing, and unchanging, and his nature defines the Good.
beliefsPage.beliefsQ3A1: Because of humanity's rebellion against God, all of creation suffers in bondage to the powers of Sin and Death, and all things were spiraling toward destruction. In Christ, God the Son entered creation as a creature, and brought God's miraculous healing, abundance, and truth to real people. He died in sacrifice to take away the sin of the world, and defeated death by rising bodily from the grave. He lives today, human and God, at the right hand of the Father, and will come again to judge the world and reign forever. Jesus is still with us by the power of the Holy Spirit, who is active in this world, continuing what he started long ago. Anyone who believes in Jesus is a new creation, forgiven of all their sin, and looks forward to the hope of resurrection and the promise of eternal life.
beliefsPage.beliefsQ3A2: John of Patmos said this of God's plan for the world to come: "I heard a loud voice from the throne, saying, 'Look! The home of God is among mortals. He will dwell with them, and they will be his peoples, and God himself will be with them and be their God'" (Rev. 21:3).
beliefsPage.fitCard1Body: We live under the authority of scripture, the true and authoritative witness to the Word of God incarnate, and interpret it by the guiding light of God revealed in Jesus, its true center. The Bible is a collection of various kinds of literature, written in many times by many people, all truly and fully inspired by God the Spirit to tell the one, unified story of God's plan to live among us, enfold us into the Triune love, and make all things new.
beliefsPage.fitCard2Body: We affirm the ecumenical creeds of the Church. We believe in God's sovereign, providential care for all things, his irrevocable choice to save, and his everlasting covenant promise to be faithful to his people. We celebrate God's glory displayed in creation, salvation, and restoration. We are led by a humble, growing tradition in the PCUSA Book of Confessions, which we accept as a reliable and faithful exposition of what scripture leads us to believe and do.
beliefsPage.fitCard3Body: We believe that correctly interpreted, scripture leads us to live out the gospel by the full and sincere welcome of women and LGBTQ people. Accordingly, we do not place restrictions of identity on the Spirit's calling to leadership, and we celebrate the gift of faithful marriage between two people of any gender.
beliefsPage.goingCard1Body: It matters that we were called to be the Church at Michigan and Cullerton, and we are committed to loving our neighbors and preaching the gospel here in the South Loop.
beliefsPage.goingCard2Body: Our congregation loves its music, liturgy, and fellowship. We are seeking to revel in the abundant life of God by offering our praise and thanksgiving and receiving the gifts of Word and Table.
beliefsPage.goingCard3Body: Community is formed in warmth and self-giving. We believe that God is at work drawing people to himself, and we continually prepare to receive, embrace, and grow into the Church of tomorrow, making disciples of all people.
beliefsPage.deeperIntro: Explore these resources, and join a community group at Second.
beliefsPage.finalCtaHeadline: The best way to know us is to worship with us
beliefsPage.finalCtaSubhead: Join us this Sunday at 11am, or reach out with any question about faith and life at Second.

musicPage.introBodyP1: Sunday worship at Second is sung. Hymns, spirituals, and anthems, accompanied by organ, carry the congregation through the liturgy week by week. Music is not a performance here. It is how we pray together.
musicPage.choirBodyP1: The quartette choir was an early American Protestant practice meant to lift the quality of sung worship. Chicago's first quartette choir was established in 1836, and Second Presbyterian followed about two decades later.
musicPage.choirBodyP2: Today our quartet is made up of classical professional vocalists who lead the congregation in hymns, anthems, and service music, week in and week out.
musicPage.organBodyP1: Our pipe organ carries salvaged parts of an 1873 Johnson & Son instrument that was lost when fire destroyed the sanctuary in 1900. The organ you hear today was completed by the Austin Organ Company of Hartford, Connecticut, in 1917.
musicPage.organBodyP2: A “thundersheet,” acquired in the 1930s and likely salvaged from a theater, still produces rolls of thunder during our annual performance of Theodore Dubois’ “The Seven Last Words of Christ.”
musicPage.finalCtaHeadline: Hear it for yourself on Sunday
musicPage.finalCtaSubhead: Worship with us at 11am, or watch the livestream online.

aboutPage.muralCaption: The painted angels of the sanctuary, the namesake of the Church of the Angels.
aboutPage.buildingBodyP1: Our sanctuary, rebuilt in 1901 in the Arts and Crafts style after fire, is home to nine Tiffany windows and a ceiling of painted angels that gave the church its nickname. Visitors travel from all over the world to see it.
aboutPage.buildingBodyP2: It is one of the great interiors in American church architecture, and it is still, first and last, a room built for worship.
aboutPage.whoHeadline: A living congregation in the South Loop
aboutPage.whoBodyP1: We are a Reformed congregation in the Presbyterian Church (USA), gathering each week to worship, love, serve, pray, and share the gospel in word and deed.
aboutPage.whoBodyP2: We welcome everyone: women and men, gay and straight, lifelong believers and the simply curious. Whoever you are, you are welcome here.
aboutPage.finalCtaHeadline: There is room for you here
aboutPage.finalCtaSubhead: Join us for worship Sundays at 11am, and see the Church of the Angels for yourself.

kidsPage.worshipBodyP1: We do not tuck children away. They worship right alongside the rest of us, and there is a children's message during the service just for them.
kidsPage.worshipBodyP2: We keep books, coloring materials, and fidget toys on hand. And if you need a quieter moment, a cry room with an audio stream of the service is always open.
kidsPage.worshipBodyP3: Bringing little ones for the first time? Come as you are. You will not be the only family in the pews, and you will not get any side-eye for the wiggles.
kidsPage.finalCtaHeadline: We would love to meet your family
kidsPage.finalCtaSubhead: Join us Sundays at 11am, or reach out with any question about visiting with children.

foodPage.lunchBagBodyP1: A grab-and-go lunch for anyone who needs one. Pantry staples, produce, clothing, and hygiene items are offered occasionally as they are available.
foodPage.tableBodyP1: A free, sit-down meal for all. Come play games, listen to music, and share a table with neighbors. Medical and social work services, occupational therapy, and clothing are available, hosted in partnership with Care for Friends. The Table pauses for the summer.
foodPage.finalCtaHeadline: Everyone is welcome at the table
foodPage.finalCtaSubhead: Come to eat, come to serve, or help keep the door open with a gift. All are needed.

givePage.onlineBodyP1: Make a one-time or recurring gift through our secure giving portal. It takes just a minute.
givePage.mailBodyP1: Prefer to send a check? Make it out to Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago and mail it to:
givePage.foodBodyP1: Want your gift to go directly to feeding our neighbors? You can designate it for Lunch Bag or the South Loop Community Table.
givePage.finalCtaHeadline: Every gift is a part of the work
givePage.finalCtaSubhead: Thank you for helping Second serve and celebrate Jesus for the good of the world.

useOurSpacePage.introHeadline: Throughout the week, our doors are open
useOurSpacePage.introBodyP1: We host all sorts of gatherings throughout the week, from youth sports and board meetings to concerts, rehearsals, social services, and 12-step groups.
useOurSpacePage.introBodyP2: You get a premium South Loop location close to public transit, competitive rates, friendly support, and first-come, first-served free parking.
useOurSpacePage.inquireIntro: Get in touch to ask about fees and availability, and we will be back in touch soon.
useOurSpacePage.finalCtaHeadline: Come see the space in person
useOurSpacePage.finalCtaSubhead: The best way to picture your event here is to experience the building. Join us for worship, or reach out to arrange a visit.

weddingsPage.pricingFootnote: The Fellowship Hall is available for receptions at an additional fee.
weddingsPage.inquireIntro: Tell us a little about your day and we will be in touch to check availability and answer your questions.
weddingsPage.finalCtaSubhead: Reach out to the office to check availability and start planning your day at Second.

contactPage.gettingHereBody: We sit on Michigan Avenue in the South Loop, close to public transit, with first-come, first-served free parking. Looking for our food ministry? Find us at the Cullerton door.
contactPage.finalCtaHeadline: We hope to see you Sunday
contactPage.finalCtaSubhead: Worship is at 11am every Sunday. Whoever you are, you are welcome here.

faqPage.heroSubhead: If your question is not here, just ask. We would love to help you feel at home before you ever walk in.
faqPage.finalCtaSubhead: The best answer to most questions is a Sunday morning. Reach out and we will help however we can.

eventsPage.finalCtaSubhead: Worship is at 11am every Sunday, and everyone is welcome at every gathering.

sermonsPage.watchHeadline: Join us for worship, wherever you are
sermonsPage.watchBody: We livestream Sunday worship and post recent messages on our YouTube channel. Watch the latest, or join us live on Sunday at 11am.
sermonsPage.finalCtaSubhead: There is nothing like being in the room. Join us Sundays at 11am at the Church of the Angels.

growPage.finalCtaSubhead: Everyone is welcome at every group. Check the calendar for the next gathering, or just show up.

servePage.serveCtaSubhead: Tell us where you would like to serve and we will help you find a place to plug in.

staffPage.finalCtaHeadline: We would love to meet you
staffPage.finalCtaSubhead: Join us for worship on Sunday, or reach out to the office any time.
